meta-harness.question: What does a meta-harness coordinate?
meta-harness.opening: A meta-harness coordinates tasks, progress, and results across agent sessions.

meta-harness.question: When should I use a meta-harness instead of a single harness?
meta-harness.opening: Use a meta-harness when you need cross-harness coordination or shared session controls that a single harness does not provide.

meta-harness.question: How does Omnigent work as a meta-harness?
meta-harness.opening: Omnigent coordinates supported agent harnesses through shared sessions; you still manage task briefs, checkout separation, and integration-specific limits.

contextual-policy.question: How does a contextual policy differ from a fixed rule?
contextual-policy.opening: An agent policy is contextual when its decision depends on session state as well as the proposed action.

contextual-policy.question: How do contextual policies compare with native agent permissions?
contextual-policy.opening: Contextual policies use session state as well as the action, while static native permissions match tools, commands, or paths.

contextual-policy.question: How do Omnigent contextual policies work?
contextual-policy.opening: Omnigent supplies a common policy event interface and persisted session state across supported integrations.

contextual-policy.question: What actions can agent policies block?
contextual-policy.opening: An agent policy can block actions at supported request or tool-call gates.

orchestrate-codex-and-claude-code.question: What does coordinating Codex and Claude Code require?
orchestrate-codex-and-claude-code.opening: Orchestrating Codex and Claude Code requires bounded tasks, explicit context handoffs, and separate checkouts for parallel writers.

orchestrate-codex-and-claude-code.question: What are the options for coordinating Codex and Claude Code?
orchestrate-codex-and-claude-code.opening: Use separate terminals when manual coordination is sufficient.

orchestrate-codex-and-claude-code.question: How can Codex and Claude Code review each other’s work?
orchestrate-codex-and-claude-code.opening: To have Codex review Claude Code’s work, or vice versa, give the reviewing agent the goal, exact checkout, base revision, changed files, and checks already run.

orchestrate-codex-and-claude-code.question: How do I launch Codex and Claude Code in Omnigent?
orchestrate-codex-and-claude-code.opening: Configure supported credentials for Claude Code and Codex during Omnigent setup, then launch their sessions through the app or web UI.

hand-off-a-session-to-a-teammate.question: What should a coding-agent handoff include?
hand-off-a-session-to-a-teammate.opening: Before taking over a coding-agent task, a teammate needs a brief naming the goal, checkout path, branch or base commit, failing or passing checks, unresolved questions, and next action.

hand-off-a-session-to-a-teammate.question: Should I share a coding-agent session or send a Git branch?
hand-off-a-session-to-a-teammate.opening: Send a Git branch or pull request when your teammate mainly needs the code; share the live coding-agent session when they need to direct the existing agent in its environment.

hand-off-a-session-to-a-teammate.question: How do I share a coding-agent session in Omnigent?
hand-off-a-session-to-a-teammate.opening: To hand off a coding-agent session in Omnigent, open Share and grant your trusted teammate Edit access to continue, or Read access to observe.

schedule-recurring-agent-tasks.question: What does a recurring coding-agent task need?
schedule-recurring-agent-tasks.opening: A recurring coding-agent task needs explicit inputs, a checkout revision or update strategy, an output location, and a stopping condition.

schedule-recurring-agent-tasks.question: How should I choose a scheduler for coding-agent tasks?
schedule-recurring-agent-tasks.opening: Choose a coding-agent scheduler by execution environment and the record you need: cron for a maintained machine, CI for repository jobs with retained logs, a hosted scheduler for cloud execution, or a session scheduler for inspectable conversations.

schedule-recurring-agent-tasks.question: How do I schedule recurring coding-agent tasks in Omnigent?
schedule-recurring-agent-tasks.opening: Ask Omnigent to create the recurring coding-agent task, or open Automations in the sidebar at /tasks and choose New automation.

schedule-recurring-agent-tasks.question: What should I check before leaving coding-agent tasks unattended?
schedule-recurring-agent-tasks.opening: Recurring coding-agent tasks need execution permissions, a verified budget policy, and checks of the actual output as well as run status.

continue-a-session-on-your-phone.question: What must stay online to use a coding agent from my phone?
continue-a-session-on-your-phone.opening: To continue a laptop coding-agent session on a phone, you need a reachable interface, access to the right account or terminal, and an execution machine that stays online.

continue-a-session-on-your-phone.question: How can I access a coding-agent session from my phone?
continue-a-session-on-your-phone.opening: SSH with a persistent terminal such as tmux is sufficient when you want the original CLI and can manage remote access.

continue-a-session-on-your-phone.question: How do I continue an Omnigent session on my phone?
continue-a-session-on-your-phone.opening: To continue a laptop coding-agent session on your phone through Omnigent, open the same reachable server in your phone browser and return to the existing session.

set-spending-limits-for-coding-agents.question: Which spending limits should I use for coding agents?
set-spending-limits-for-coding-agents.opening: Choose coding-agent spending controls by scope: a run limit for one task, an agent policy for managed sessions, or provider controls for account-wide spending.

set-spending-limits-for-coding-agents.question: How do I cap coding-agent spending in Omnigent?
set-spending-limits-for-coding-agents.opening: To cap a coding-agent session’s recorded spending in Omnigent, attach a cost_budget policy to the session, declare it in an agent specification, or use applicable administrator policies.

set-spending-limits-for-coding-agents.question: How do Omnigent spending checkpoints and hard caps work?
set-spending-limits-for-coding-agents.opening: An Omnigent session’s soft spending checkpoint returns ASK at the next supported gate; an all-model hard cap on the root session (the original conversation) returns DENY.

set-spending-limits-for-coding-agents.question: What spending does each Omnigent budget cover?
set-spending-limits-for-coding-agents.opening: Omnigent child-agent budgets cover a delegated subtree, user budgets span sessions, and scheduled-task caps are requested per firing, with best-effort attachment in v0.19.0.
